install.title: Quickstart
install.html:
Path 1: Fully Hosted Cloud

Scale browser automation with our hosted agent, stealth browsers, and infrastructure for profiles, recordings, and data policies.

Get started with the API ↗

New Google, GitHub, or Microsoft signups get $1 cloud credit.


Path 2: CLI

Paste this prompt into Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, or your favorite agent.

Install browser-use with `uv tool install browser-use==1.0.8`, run `browser-use skill install` to register the skill, and connect it to my browser. If setup or connection fails, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.

Path 3: Python Library

browser-use 1.0. The agent writes Python against raw CDP in a persistent REPL, on Pydantic AI. Coming from 0.x? Read MIGRATING.md.

Python 3.11 or newer. Get an API key at Browser Use Cloud, then install with uv, or pip in a venv:

uv init --python 3.12 my-agent && cd my-agent
uv add 'browser-use==1.0.8'
uv run browser-use login             # sign in once; the key is saved (over SSH: --device-code)

python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install 'browser-use==1.0.8'
browser-use login

Or set BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=bu_... (a key from https://cloud.browser-use.com/new-api-key). In a notebook: browser_use.login().

Pin the exact version (==, never >=). browser-use moves fast and releases can break things. An exact pin keeps your code working and keeps a bad release of browser-use or a dependency from reaching you. Upgrade on purpose, after reading the release notes.

from browser_use import Agent

result = Agent('Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo').run_sync()
print(result.final_result())

Defaults: model bu-4.0 (BU 4.0) on the Browser Use gateway, browser = a Browser Use Cloud browser (stopped when the run ends). One key pays for the model and the cloud browser (also ChatBrowserUse(api_key=...)'s), and also works for the CLI and MCP server. A .env file works too.

Without a key, an interactive desktop run opens Browser Use login and continues after approval. Over SSH or on Linux without a desktop it prints a link and a code to approve on any device, then continues. Login creates and saves the key automatically; no copying is needed. Ctrl-C stops it with the missing-key error. Set BROWSER_USE_AUTO_LOGIN=false to disable automatic login (=true allows the device code in a container). Servers, CI, notebooks, containers and piped input keep the missing-key error and the browser-use login instructions.

Cloud browsers print their interactive live-view link to stderr by default. Use Browser(live_view=True) to open it automatically, or Browser(live_view=False) to hide it. Anyone with the link can control the browser.

With telemetry enabled, anonymous library_auth events record missing keys, login outcomes, available keys, and browser starts. These events use the existing installation ID and contain no API keys, login URLs, or account identifiers (fields: Telemetry below). Key availability does not prove that the server accepts the key. Cloud browser startup confirms that authentication worked.

Local browser, your model:

from browser_use import Agent, Browser, ChatOpenAI

agent = Agent(
    'Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo',
    llm=ChatOpenAI('gpt-6-luna'),        # OPENAI_API_KEY; or ChatOpenAI(model, base_url=...) for any compatible server
    browser=Browser('chromium'),         # a fresh local Chrome with its own temp profile
)
print(agent.run_sync().final_result())  # in async code: result = await agent.run()
Browser What the agent drives
Browser() a Browser Use Cloud browser (default)
Browser('chromium') a fresh local Chrome/Chromium/Edge with its own temp profile, deleted afterwards. Headless when there is no display (Docker, CI); headless=, executable_path=, user_data_dir= (a profile dir kept between runs)
Browser('chrome') the Chrome you have open, with your logins (turn on chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging once)
Browser('chrome', profile='Work') a new Chrome on a temporary copy of your Chrome profile Work (sync off); your Chrome can stay open, except on Windows

Other models: ChatAnthropic, ChatGoogle (both built in), or any Pydantic AI model string such as llm='groq:llama-3.3-70b-versatile' (after pip install 'pydantic-ai-slim[groq]').
